title: Remove Duplicates from Sorted List
spaceBreakdown:
- ListNode* cur: one pointer → O(1)
- recursion depth: none
- not counted: input list, returned head
approach: Since the list is sorted, all duplicates are adjacent. Walk a single pointer through the list; whenever the current node's value equals its successor's, relink `cur->next` past the duplicate (and re-check without advancing, since several duplicates may chain). Otherwise advance. This relinks in place, so the head never changes and we return it directly.
hints: The list is already sorted in ascending order. Where must any two equal values be located relative to each other?
Single pointer traversal. With head = [1,1,2], at the first node (value 1) its successor also has value 1, so relink `cur->next` to skip that successor, yielding [1,2].

**Empty list** - no nodes at all.
`Input: []` → `Expected: []`
⚠️ Bug: dereferencing `head` without a null guard → crash / null-pointer dereference.

**Single node** - only one element, nothing to compare against.
`Input: [5]` → `Expected: [5]`
⚠️ Bug: accessing `cur->next->val` before checking `cur->next != null` → null-pointer dereference.

**All equal** - every node has the same value.
`Input: [2,2,2]` → `Expected: [2]`
⚠️ Bug: advancing `cur` immediately after relinking instead of re-checking → returns `[2,2]` (one duplicate survives).

**No duplicates** - already distinct values.
`Input: [1,2,3]` → `Expected: [1,2,3]`
⚠️ Bug: relinking `cur->next` unconditionally even when values differ → list gets truncated to `[1]`.

followUps.q: What if the list were NOT sorted - how would you remove duplicates?
followUps.a: You could no longer rely on adjacency, so track seen values in a hash set while walking once; skip any node whose value is already in the set. Time O(n), space O(n).

followUps.q: Instead of keeping one copy, remove EVERY node whose value appears more than once (keep only truly-unique values)?
followUps.a: Use a dummy head and a `prev` pointer; when you detect a run of equal values, relink `prev->next` past the entire run. Still O(n) time and O(1) space because the list is sorted.

followUps.q: What if the list arrives as a stream and you cannot store it all at once?
followUps.a: This solution already works: it only ever compares the current node with its immediate successor, so it needs O(1) memory and one forward pass regardless of list length.
